                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">And after the league <ns0:hi>made</ns0:hi> with him, he shall work deceitfully <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">For he made a league with <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and came with a few in comparison, (but they were chosen men) and he took the passes and set Garrisons, and put all in subjection to him.</ns0:note>: for he shall come up, and shall become strong with a small people.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 He shall enter <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>into the peaceable and fat,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> peaceably even upon the fattest places of the province <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">He shall come in upon the <ns0:hi>Egyptians</ns0:hi> under pretence of peace, and in time of Peace, to a secure People in a plentiful, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />licious Countrey, and among a mass of Treasures which the Kings successively had heaped up, the greatest part of which this <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> took and distributed among his chiefest Confidents whereby he obliged them the faster to him, for he was large hearted and liberal. He did herein (saith the Text) <ns0:hi>what his Fathers had not done,</ns0:hi> the Kings of <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> before him could never attain to this success over <ns0:hi>Aegypt,</ns0:hi> as he did.</ns0:note>, and he shall do <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> which his fathers have not done, nor his fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers fathers, he shall scatter among them the prey and spoil, and riches; <ns0:hi>yea,</ns0:hi> and he shall <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>think his thoughts.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> forecast his devices against the strong-holds <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Having succeeded thus far in the lesser places of the Countrey he shall proceed to the most important Cities and Places of greatest strength in that Kingdom.</ns0:note>, even for a time <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">That is till God put a stop to his carriere, for he held <ns0:hi>Aegypt</ns0:hi> not long, the <ns0:hi>Aegyptians</ns0:hi> found means to deliver themselves from his yoke when their King grew to riper years, yet against this did <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> fore-cast his devices, as saith the Text.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:144" />25 And he shall stir up his power and his cou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rage against the king of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>outh with a great army <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Antiochus Epiphanes</ns0:hi> being emboldned by his former successes shall wage War against <ns0:hi>Ptolomy</ns0:hi> King of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> with all his might, and with open force.</ns0:note>, and the king of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>outh shall be stir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red up to battel with a very great and mighty army <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Being exasperated against <ns0:hi>Antiochus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>; but he shall not stand: for they shall forecast devices against him <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He might have prospered, if he had not been betrayed by <ns0:hi>Eulaius, Lenaeus,</ns0:hi> and the rest of his Nobles being corrupted by <ns0:hi>Antiochus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Yea, they that feed of the portion of his meat, shall destroy him <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">His most familiar Friends and Confidents, shall be False and Treacherous to him, for he shall be overthrown with a great slaughter, as when <ns0:hi>Nilus</ns0:hi> overflows the Countrey, for there was the Battle between mount <ns0:hi>Casius</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pelusium.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and his army shall overflow: and many shall fall down slain.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And both these kings <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>their hearts.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> hearts <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> to do mischief, and they shall speak lies at one table <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">They shall meet under pretence of Peace, but with trea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cherous intents on both sides; they both plaid the Gipsies with each other at <ns0:hi>Memphis,</ns0:hi> where <ns0:hi>Ptolomy</ns0:hi> invited <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> to a feast, these interviews of Neighbour Kings jealous one of another, have ever proved fatal; though under the smoothest promises.</ns0:note>, but it shall not prosper <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">For neither shall <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> gain <ns0:hi>Aegypt</ns0:hi> by all his Artifice, nor <ns0:hi>Ptolomy Syria.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>; for yet the end <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> at the time appointed <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> By the Lord whose purpose and counsel shall stand, whatever the devices of mens Hearts are.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Then shall he return into his land with great riches <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> shall depart with his booty gotten in <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> into his Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> and be content with the bounds of that, leav<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:hi>Aegypt</ns0:hi> behind him.</ns0:note>, and his heart <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> against the holy covenant <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Against the Law and Covenant of God, with the people that Worshipped God according to his Rule, and Will.</ns0:note>: and he shall do <ns0:hi>exploits,</ns0:hi> and return to his own land <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He shall greatly afflict and vex the People of God, yet was it a mercy they had this warning of this sore tryal. <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> was a fit instrument of the Devil for this work, being rich and proud, and thought he might take this in his way: God permitting this horn to push and gore, for his peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples sins, and for a preparation to his own ruine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 At the time appointed he shall return, and come toward the south <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e. Aegypt,</ns0:hi> to fight against <ns0:hi>Ptolomy</ns0:hi> and his Wife <ns0:hi>Cleopatra,</ns0:hi> Sister to <ns0:hi>Antiochus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, but it shall not be as the former, or as the latter <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">This shall not be so prosperous as the two former Expeditions, but shall fail of his victory and booty.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 For the ships of Chittim shall come against him <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> out of <ns0:hi>Italy,</ns0:hi> and parts of the <ns0:hi>Archipelago,</ns0:hi> under them shall come with force and they shall vex and afflict him; for the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> had Harbours for their Ships and Gallies in <ns0:hi>Cilicia, Macedonia</ns0:hi> and other Parts of those Coasts; whereby after they had subdued <ns0:hi>Greece,</ns0:hi> they pursued <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Asia,</ns0:hi> and sent into <ns0:hi>Aegypt</ns0:hi> to prevent his going into <ns0:hi>Alexandria, Liv. l.</ns0:hi> 45. This grieved and fretted him: For when he lingred and framed excuses, <ns0:hi>Popilius</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Embassador made a Circle about him with his rod, commanding he should not stir thence till he gave him a positive present answer, by which sore against his will he was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ain to pack away out of <ns0:hi>Aegypt,</ns0:hi> and withdraw his Garrisons and Navy thence. This made his heart boyl with rancor, which he spit out all against the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> therefore its said, <ns0:hi>he shall, &c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: therefore he shall be grieved and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turn, and have indignation against the holy co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Especially being sollicited to it by <ns0:hi>Iason</ns0:hi> first, and <ns0:hi>Menelaus</ns0:hi> after, who were Apostates, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trayers of their Brethren, and the true Worship of God, 2 <ns0:hi>Mac.</ns0:hi> 4.26, 27, &c. because <ns0:hi>Onias</ns0:hi> was in power, this they envyed, therefore went to <ns0:hi>Antiochus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: so shall he do, he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And arms shall stand on his part, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 8.11. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 12.11.</ns0:note> they shall pollute the sanctuary <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 24.21.</ns0:note> of strength <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e. Antiochus</ns0:hi> shall come with armed power to assist the desertors, and force the faithful <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> by his Garrisons.</ns0:note>, and shall take away the daily <ns0:hi>sacrifice</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">For he polluted the Sanctuary by taking away the Holy vessels, and forbidding the publick Worship, but he added a third pollution, by setting up in the Temple the <ns0:hi>abomination of desolation, i. e.</ns0:hi> The abominable Idol of <ns0:hi>Iupiter Olympius,</ns0:hi> with many more, 1 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 1.21, 22, 23, 41, <ns0:hi>to the end.</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 5.24.</ns0:note>, and they shall place the abomination that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> maketh de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solate.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And such as do wickedly against the cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant, shall he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> corrupt by flatteries <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">For by Gifts, Preferments, and Promises he drew away great multitudes of this wretched people of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> alwayes bent to backsliding, to his Idololatrical and Heathenish practises and interest.</ns0:note>: but the people <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                           <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> that do know their God, shall be strong, and do <ns0:hi>exploits</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">They that adhere to the true Worship of God and are zealous for it, shall scorn <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi>'s Gifts, and abhorr his Ways, and defie his force, not loving their Lives to the Death; as you have many instances, 1 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 1.62, 63. 2 <ns0:hi>Macc. chap.</ns0:hi> 5, 6, 7, 8. and also how <ns0:hi>Iudas Maccabeus</ns0:hi> and his few followers did exploits against <ns0:hi>Nicanor</ns0:hi> and others.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And they that understand among the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, shall instruct many <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Such as <ns0:hi>Eleazar</ns0:hi> that old Scribe, 2 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 6.18. and some others Learned in the Lawes of God, and Holy in Heart, and Life shall instruct many in the Righteous ways of God, and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain them from Apostacy when others fall off.</ns0:note>: yet they shall fall by the sword, and by flame, by captivity, and by spoil <ns0:hi>many</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> & 10.4<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> days <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Many of the People shall fall, yea of their pious and learned Teachers, as well as their Disciples, 1 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 1.52, 66. 2 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Now when they shall fall, they shall be holpen with a little help: but many shall cleave to them with flatteries <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> God in their affliction when it is great, wherein he never leaves himself without witness, shall raise up some suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cour, to be witnesses to this Truth, to vindicate his honour and save his people from utter destruction, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Maccabus.</ns0:hi> Read what <ns0:hi>Mattathias</ns0:hi> and his Sons did at <ns0:hi>Modin,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Macc.</ns0:hi> 2. read the chapter, who would not be flattered out of their Reli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> of them of understanding shall fall <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note>, to try <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> them <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">We see hereby that the best of men have some drosse, which makes afflictions, yea fiery trials necessary for them, for the word signifies all kind of examination and tryals, either as Founders try Mettals to purge them, or as Corn is winnowed to cleanse it from chaff, or as Fullers that wash and scour to take out spots, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 3.1, 2, 3.</ns0:note>, and to purge, and to make <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> white, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> to the time of the end: because <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> yet for a time appointed <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Now mark here the spirit of God seems to slide into the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Monarchy, for this began in the Reign of <ns0:hi>Antiochus,</ns0:hi> so that he did begin that which the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> afterward in process of time acted more highly against the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> too. For <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> is made by all a Type of <ns0:hi>An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tichrist</ns0:hi>; as <ns0:hi>Maldonate</ns0:hi> confesseth, and thus you find the Prophets, and our Saviour too; <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> brings in Christ, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 72.8. when the rest is spoken of <ns0:hi>Solomon.</ns0:hi> So <ns0:hi>Ps.</ns0:hi> 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sa.</ns0:hi> 49, 54, and 60. So our Saviour speaking of the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> speaks with it of the end of the World, and thus the end of this chapter is clearly of <ns0:hi>Anti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />christ,</ns0:hi> and this Prophesie of <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> ends with the Worlds end. Therefore <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> is a Type of <ns0:hi>Antichrist,</ns0:hi> in his Pride, Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness, Craft, and Cruelty against the People of God, and blasphemies and Idolatries to the reproach of <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi> Therefore it is here added, <ns0:hi>because it is yet for the time appointed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And the king <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The King, i. e.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Government, whether by the <ns0:hi>Senate,</ns0:hi> or by <ns0:hi>Emperours,</ns0:hi> or by the <ns0:hi>Bishop of Rome,</ns0:hi> who shall shove out the <ns0:hi>Imperial</ns0:hi> Power not only from <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> but from <ns0:hi>Italy,</ns0:hi> and all the <ns0:hi>Western</ns0:hi> Empire as far as he could by striking in with the barbarous Nations that invaded it, who are called <ns0:hi>Ten Kings.</ns0:hi> Read for all this <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 17.10, 11, 12, 13. as all the seven or eight Governments of <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> are called <ns0:hi>Horns,</ns0:hi> and the Horns, <ns0:hi>Kings, ver.</ns0:hi> 10, 11. The summe is this, though it is granted some of these things are applicable to <ns0:hi>Anti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>chus,</ns0:hi> yet the Angel speaks of him here and henceforward, but by the by and very lightly. His main scope is <ns0:hi>Antichrist,</ns0:hi> as will appear in the interpretation.</ns0:note> shall do according to his will <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> did according to his Will: he shall be Arbitrary in his actions notwithstanding any cl<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ecks of Divine and humane Laws, the cause follows.</ns0:note>, and he shall exalt himself, and magnifie himself above every god, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> & 8.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> shall speak marvellous things against the GOD of Gods <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This is true of the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> who would deifie what they please, and d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>fie it or ungod it. Most true of the Persecutors of Christ, and Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans in the time of the <ns0:hi>Emperours,</ns0:hi> but most notoriously of the <ns0:hi>Ro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> Antichrist. See how this agrees with that Prophesie. 2 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 2.3, 4. to verse 10. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 17.3.</ns0:note>, and shall prosper till the indignation be ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complished <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Then shall An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tichrist continue long and prevail, read for this, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>pe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>

                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>m.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: for that that is determined shall be done <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">That which God hath decreed to be done by him against the Saints shall be done, and that which God hath pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed to be done upon him, shall be executed also to his de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:144" />37 Neither shall he regard the God of his fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">He shall so far degenerate from the rule of Christ, and from primitive Christianity, that he shall be the head of that <ns0:hi>Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stacy,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.1. 2 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 2.3. mark those places, the first whereof is so fully opened by Mr. <ns0:hi>Ioseph Mede</ns0:hi> in his Doctrine of <ns0:hi>Daemons.</ns0:hi> The other by Bishop <ns0:hi>Iewel</ns0:hi> in his Com. on that place.</ns0:note>, nor the desire of women <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The desire of Wiving, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> forbidding to Marry, for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bidding Priests marriage.</ns0:note>, nor regard any god for he shall magnifie himself above all.</ns0:p>

                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">

                     </ns0:gap>

                     <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>zzim</ns0:hi> of strengths or strong holds, the <ns0:hi>Phaenicians</ns0:hi> Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipped <ns0:hi>Mars</ns0:hi> the God of Wars, which <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi> did Worship but we are come to the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi>; and though many have con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jectured several senses of this <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
